yared.name: Yared
yared.summary: Aksumite composer and scholar (505–571) credited with inventing traditional Ethiopian church music, its notation system, and the Zema chant tradition still performed today.

debre-dammo.name: Debre Damo
debre-dammo.summary: A steep, flat-topped mountain in Ethiopia's Tigray Region, home to a 6th-century monastery accessible only by rope, said to hold the country's oldest surviving church building.

zagwe-dynasty.name: Zagwe dynasty
zagwe-dynasty.summary: A medieval Agaw monarchy ruling parts of Ethiopia and Eritrea from about 1137 to 1270 CE, famed for King Lalibela's rock-hewn churches; its last king, Za-Ilmaknun, was killed in battle.

tigray-region.name: Tigray Region
tigray-region.summary: The northernmost regional state of Ethiopia, homeland of the Tigrayan, Irob and Kunama peoples, with Mekelle as its capital.

lalibela.name: Lalibela
lalibela.summary: A town in Ethiopia's Amhara Region famed for rock-cut monolithic churches traditionally dated to the reign of King Gebre Meskel Lalibela (r. c. 1181-1221); one of Ethiopia's holiest pilgrimage sites.

kaleb-of-axum.name: Kaleb of Axum
kaleb-of-axum.summary: A king of Aksum, a kingdom in what is now Ethiopia and Eritrea, also known and venerated under other names including Saint Elesbaan and Ella Asbeha.

gebre-meskel-lalibela.name: Gebre Meskel Lalibela
gebre-meskel-lalibela.summary: King of Ethiopia's Zagwe dynasty from 1181 to 1221, credited as the patron of the rock-hewn churches of Lalibela and venerated as a saint by the Ethiopian Orthodox Church.

axum.name: Axum
axum.summary: A town in Ethiopia's Tigray Region, once capital of the ancient Aksumite Empire, and a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1980 for its archaeological importance.

pillar-tomb.name: Pillar tomb
pillar-tomb.summary: A type of monumental grave whose central feature is a single, prominent stone pillar or column.

kingdom-of-aksum.name: Kingdom of Aksum
kingdom-of-aksum.summary: A powerful trading kingdom in the Horn of Africa and South Arabia, founded around the 1st century, ranked among the era's four great powers, and one of the first states to adopt Christianity, in the 4th century.

gudit.name: Gudit
gudit.summary: A 10th-century queen said to have ravaged the Kingdom of Aksum and destroyed its churches, known under several names and surviving mainly in Horn of Africa folklore.

agaw-people.name: Agaw
agaw-people.summary: A Cushitic ethnic group of Ethiopia's northern highlands and Eritrea, speaking the Agaw (Central Cushitic) languages; many historically practiced a 'Hebraic religion' and included Beta Israel Jews.

banu-makhzum.name: Banu Makhzum
banu-makhzum.summary: One of the wealthiest and most powerful clans of the Quraysh in Mecca before Islam, alongside the Banu Hashim and Banu Umayya.

ifat-historical-region.name: Ifat
ifat-historical-region.summary: A historical Muslim region in the Horn of Africa, located on the eastern edge of Shewa.

shewa.name: Shewa
shewa.summary: A historical region of Ethiopia, once an autonomous kingdom within the Ethiopian Empire, whose territory includes the modern capital Addis Ababa.

garima-gospels.name: Garima Gospels
garima-gospels.summary: Three ancient Ge'ez manuscripts of the four Gospels, the earliest possibly composed around 500 CE, making them the oldest surviving Ethiopian manuscripts of any kind.

ge-ez.name: Ge'ez
ge-ez.summary: Ancient South Semitic language from Ethiopia and Eritrea, still used today as the liturgical language of Ethiopian and Eritrean Orthodox and Catholic churches.

ge-ez-script.name: Ge'ez script
ge-ez-script.summary: Writing system originating in Ethiopia and Eritrea, first used to write the Geʽez language and later adapted for Amharic, Tigrinya and other languages.

solomonic-dynasty.name: Solomonic dynasty
solomonic-dynasty.summary: Ruling dynasty of the Ethiopian Empire from the 13th to 20th centuries, founded in 1270 by Yekuno Amlak and claiming descent from the biblical Solomon; ended in 1974 with Haile Selassie's overthrow.

tekle-haymanot.name: Tekle Haymanot
tekle-haymanot.summary: An Ethiopian saint and monk (1215–1313) venerated as a hermit, who founded a major monastery in his native Shewa and served as Abuna of Ethiopia. He is the only Ethiopian saint celebrated officially in foreign churches such as Rome and Egypt.

ishaaq-bin-ahmed.name: Sheikh Ishaaq
ishaaq-bin-ahmed.summary: Semi-legendary Islamic scholar said to have traveled from Arabia to the Horn of Africa in the 10th or 11th century and settled at Maydh, traditionally regarded as forefather of the Somali Isaaq clan-family.

maydh.name: Maydh
maydh.summary: An ancient port city in Somaliland's eastern Sanaag region, where the semi-legendary 10th-century Sheikh Ishaaq is said to have settled after crossing from Arabia.

dil-na-od.name: Dil Na'od
dil-na-od.summary: Last king of Aksum before the Zagwe dynasty, ruling in the 9th or 10th century; according to one tradition, he was defeated by the prince Mara Takla Haymanot, who married his daughter.

mara-takla-haymanot.name: Mara Takla Haymanot
mara-takla-haymanot.summary: King who founded Ethiopia's Zagwe dynasty; some king lists call him simply "Mararah" or "Takla Haymanot."

al-ya-qubi.name: Al-Ya'qubi
al-ya-qubi.summary: An Arab Muslim historian and geographer who died in 897/8.

adal-sultanate.name: Adal Sultanate
adal-sultanate.summary: Medieval Muslim empire in the Horn of Africa, flourishing roughly 1415–1577, whose long wars with Christian Abyssinia drew in Ottoman and Portuguese forces.

zeila.name: Zeila
zeila.summary: A historic port town in what is now Somaliland, capital of the early Adal Kingdom by the 9th century and the Ifat Sultanate in the 13th, later under Ottoman and then British control.

beta-israel.name: Beta Israel
beta-israel.summary: Jewish community originating in the Amhara and Tigray regions of northern Ethiopia, historically practicing a distinct non-Talmudic form of Judaism; most have emigrated to Israel since 1979.

abyssinia.name: Abyssinia
abyssinia.summary: A historical name for a region in the Horn of Africa, roughly modern Ethiopia and Eritrea, used internationally as a synonym for Ethiopia until the mid-20th century.

habesha-peoples.name: Habesha
habesha-peoples.summary: A cultural and historical identifier, also known by the exonym Abyssinians, that historically referred mainly to the Amhara, Tigrayan-Tigrinya and Gurage peoples rather than one single ethnic group.

enno-littmann.name: Enno Littmann
enno-littmann.summary: German orientalist (1875–1958) who deciphered the Safaitic script and other ancient inscriptions, led the 1906 German Aksum expedition, and translated One Thousand and One Nights.

fatagar.name: Fatagar
fatagar.summary: A historical province in the medieval Horn of Africa that separated Muslim and Christian territories, later becoming a central district and birthplace of Ethiopian emperors in the 15th century.

sultanate-of-ifat.name: Sultanate of Ifat
sultanate-of-ifat.summary: Medieval Muslim state in the Horn of Africa, also called Wafāt or the Kingdom of Zeila, ruled by the Walashma dynasty between the late 13th and early 15th centuries.

dawaro.name: Dawaro
dawaro.summary: A Muslim principality in the Horn of Africa that became a vassal, then a province, of Ethiopia under Emperor Amda Seyon I in the early 14th century.

ethiopian-orthodox-tewahedo-church.name: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church
ethiopian-orthodox-tewahedo-church.summary: The largest Oriental Orthodox church, tracing back to the Christianization of Aksum in 330 CE, with tens of millions of adherents and one of only a few Oriental Orthodox churches in Africa.

coptic-orthodox-church.name: Coptic Orthodox Church
coptic-orthodox-church.summary: An Oriental Orthodox Christian church based in Egypt, traditionally founded by Saint Mark around AD 42, and the largest Christian group in Egypt and the Middle East.

kassala.name: Kassala
kassala.summary: The capital of Kassala state in eastern Sudan, on the Gash River, known for its fruit gardens and as a market and trade hub near the Eritrean border.

welkait.name: Welkait
welkait.summary: A woreda (district) in the Western Zone of Ethiopia's Tigray region, bordered by Humera, Tsegede and the North Gondar Zone.

walashma-dynasty.name: Walashma dynasty
walashma-dynasty.summary: A medieval Muslim dynasty founded in the 13th century in Ifat, ruling territory in the Horn of Africa now part of Somalia, Djibouti, Eritrea and eastern Ethiopia.

sultanate-of-shewa.name: Sultanate of Shewa
sultanate-of-shewa.summary: Muslim kingdom in present-day Ethiopia founded by the Arab Makhzumi dynasty, whose rise coincided with the decline of the Kingdom of Axum.

enrico-cerulli.name: Enrico Cerulli
enrico-cerulli.summary: Italian scholar of Somali and Ethiopian studies, as well as a governor and diplomat during and after Italian Fascism, who lived from 1898 to 1988.

yusuf-bin-ahmad-al-kawneyn.name: Aw Barkhadle
yusuf-bin-ahmad-al-kawneyn.summary: 10th-century Islamic scholar and traveler based in Zeila, Somalia, popularly known as 'Aw Barkhadle,' meaning 'Blessed Father.'

aw-barkhadle.name: Aw-Barkhadle
aw-barkhadle.summary: A town near Hargeisa in modern Somaliland that served as capital of the Adal Sultanate and burial place for rulers of the Walashma dynasty.

philotheos-greek-patriarch-of-alexandria.name: Philotheos of Alexandria
philotheos-greek-patriarch-of-alexandria.summary: Greek Patriarch of Alexandria from 1435 to 1459.

muhammad.name: Muhammad
muhammad.summary: The founder of Islam, born around 570 CE in Mecca, whom Muslims believe received revelations from God beginning around 610 as the final prophet.

nine-saints.name: Nine Saints
nine-saints.summary: A group of missionaries from the Byzantine Empire important to the early growth of Christianity in Ethiopia in the late 5th century.

patristics.name: Patristics
patristics.summary: The study of early Christian writers known as Church Fathers, covering the Patristic era from about 100 CE to the mid-5th or late-8th century.

kaldi.name: Kaldi
kaldi.summary: A legendary goatherd credited in popular tradition with discovering coffee around 850 CE, after which it spread to the Islamic world and beyond.

keffa-zone.name: Keffa Zone
keffa-zone.summary: An administrative zone in Ethiopia's South West Region, centered on Bonga, where Ethiopian tradition places the legendary origin of coffee drinking.

hijrah.name: Hijrah
hijrah.summary: The 622 CE journey of Muhammad and his followers from Mecca to Medina after years of persecution, marking the start of the Islamic calendar.

masjid-al-qiblatayn-zeila.name: Masjid al-Qiblatayn, Zeila
masjid-al-qiblatayn-zeila.summary: A former, now partly ruined mosque in Zeila, Somaliland, whose name reflects the belief that it was once aligned toward both Mecca and Jerusalem.
